messages:
Maria: Heads up — seeing a ~3x p95 latency jump in ap-jkt-1 starting 10:12 UTC. Kernel selector is flip-flopping and KV cache evictions spiked. Opening a thread to coordinate quick triage.
Vikram: looking at dashboards now, grabbing traces. Any deploys around 10:00–10:10?
InfraBot: alert: region=ap-jkt-1 metric=latency.p95 change=+300% window=5m triggered_at=1759001160
Jess: no infra deploys scheduled, but runtime team did ship kernel-selector heuristic tweak in canary at 09:58 UTC (commit: https://git.internal/runtime/commit/3f2e9b).
Sam: I rolled the heuristic to 10% of hosts in ap pools, not jkt specifically but routing may have drifted. Will check rollout map.
Lee: mtr from a node to nearest LDNS shows path change at ~10:11 UTC, high loss on hop 5 -> 6. paste: mtr report attached:
```
Start: Mon Mar 10 10:15:27 2025
HOST: node-az1-03
1. 10.0.0.1
2. 203.0.113.5
3. 198.51.100.9  0.5%  12ms
4. 192.0.2.1    0.0%  18ms
5. 198.51.100.25 20% 120ms
6. 203.0.113.45  45% 250ms  (packet loss spike)
...
```
Vikram: interesting — packet loss and higher RTT to LDNS would increase DNS resolution jitter and could affect kernel scoring if heuristics weight RTT. Also KV cache eviction pattern shows many small prefixes evicted: eviction log sample:
```
[10:12:05] evict key prefix=k:v:conv:1234 size=6KB reason=pressure
[10:12:06] evict key prefix=k:v:conv:5678 size=4KB reason=pressure
[10:12:07] evict key prefix=k:v:conv:abcd size=8KB reason=pressure
```
Maria: kv cache thrash coincides with kernel selector oscillation in profiler: selector scores are swinging between kernel-A and kernel-B every 200ms. That triggers different batching paths and causes serialization stalls.
Sam: could be noisy tenant VMs causing CPU steal on some hosts — check host-level procsteal.
Jess: I pulled host metrics: procsteal for several hosts in ap-jkt-1 spiked to 18%-25% at 10:10–10:14. Network PI also shows an upstream ISP flap.
NOC: we see provider flapping at IX peer ASN 64500 around that time, escalated to provider.
Lee: hypothesis: upstream peering issue increases RTT/loss -> DNS and network variance -> kernel selector (which uses recent RTT/batch success) flips kernels -> KV cache policy thrashes because different kernels warm caches differently -> tail latency spikes. Noisy tenant CPU steal amplifies selector instability.
Vikram: agreed. Short-term mitigation: 1) pin kernel selector back to stable heuristic on ap-jkt-1, 2) increase KV cache grace TTL to avoid immediate evictions during transients, 3) throttle new tenant spin-ups in the POP. I can flip safe flags.
Sam: I can run the flag to pin kernels: `POST /admin/flags/pin_kernel {"region":"ap-jkt-1","kernel":"kernel-A","duration_s":900}` — doing it now.
InfraBot: flag change applied by Sam at 1759001265: pin_kernel(region=ap-jkt-1,kernel=kernel-A,duration=900s)
Vikram: patched KV cache TTL on the control plane for ap-jkt-1 to +30s grace window. Command: `ccachectl set ap-jkt-1 grace_ttl 30s` — applied at 1759001280.
Jess: also gating canary rollout in other AP regions until provider confirms peering stability. I paused 2 scheduled batches.
Maria: after flags: p95 dropped from 3x to ~1.2x within 90s, eviction rate normalized. Observability traces show batching path stabilized.
Lee: follow-up: need a post-incident perf profile comparing kernel selection score deltas pre/post, and a kv-cache warmup heatmap for the transient. I can collect hotspot flamegraphs from affected hosts.
Vikram: I'll open a perf job: `perf/collect --region ap-jkt-1 --tags kernel-selector,kv-evict --since 1759001000 --until 1759001500` and attach results.
NOC: provider reports BGP flap resolved at 10:30 UTC and they're monitoring.
Sam: next actions: 1) revert pinned flag after 15m if stable, 2) add stabilizer to kernel selector so it requires 3 consecutive samples before switching, 3) add softhold on kv-cache evictions when selector flips. I'll draft RFC.
Maria: noted. Thanks all — good quick coordination. If latency creeps again we'll reopen and consider emergency rollback of the heuristic commit. :thumbsup:
